Domain is linear-elastic, small-deformation solid mechanics under Euler-Bernoulli beam theory.
The beam has a rectangular cross-section with width b = 50 mm and height h = 120 mm.
The cross-section is symmetric about the horizontal centroidal axis, which serves as the neutral axis.
The loading is pure bending: an internal bending moment M = 4,000,000 N·mm (sagging, taken as positive) acts at the section of interest.
No transverse shear force, axial force, distributed load, point load, or other loading is present.
The second moment of area about the neutral axis is I = b·h³/12 = 50 × 120³ / 12 = 7,200,000 mm⁴.
The flexure formula governing the bending stress at any fiber is σ = −M·y / I, where y is the signed distance from the neutral axis, positive upward.
Evaluate the bending stress at three fiber locations: y = 0 (neutral axis), y = +h/2 = +60 mm (top fiber), and y = −h/2 = −60 mm (bottom fiber).
The expected results are σ = 0 MPa at the neutral axis, σ = −33.33 MPa (compression) at the top fiber, and σ = +33.33 MPa (tension) at the bottom fiber.
All quantities are expressed in the consistent unit system of N, mm, and MPa.
Assume plane sections remain plane and perpendicular to the beam axis after deformation.
Assume the material is homogeneous, isotropic, and operates within its linear-elastic range, so Hooke's law applies.
Assume the beam is prismatic over the section of interest and the moment is constant across the cross-section (no warping or shear-lag effects).
Present the derivation by stating the flexure formula, substituting I = b·h³/12, and then evaluating σ at each of the three y-locations with the given numerical values.
